Czerwinsk Nad Wisla Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Czerwińsk nad Wisłą, Poland

Demolished. Czerwińsk, founded in 1363, saw Jewish settlement begin at the end of the 18th century; the community grew from 72 in 1808 to 425 (nearly 25% of the population) before WWII. A ghetto held roughly 3,400 Jews from Czerwińsk and nearby towns including Wyszogród and Warsaw, before deportation to the Nowy Dwór Ghetto and then Auschwitz-Birkenau in 1941-1942. This old cemetery, established in the first half of the 19th century, was destroyed during the war; the land was later designated for housing development, and no tombstones or layout traces survive.
